Extensive real-schema-vs-legacy-schema comparison (products/product_folders/inventory_movements vs items/item_folders/stock_movements + all item satellite tables, fields verified via live DESCRIBE, not guessed). Reached design decisions with the user: (1) restore sku_code/cost_per_unit/vat_type/senior_pwd_discount_eligible/description/unit_of_measure as real typed columns on products (universal to any item type); (2) add ONE products.attributes JSON column for everything else variable/category-specific (nutrition, allergens, packaging, physical properties, regulatory compliance, quality control, cost breakdown, shelf life, barcodes array, min_threshold, purchase_allowance) -- rejected EAV table and rejected rigid per-concern tables, following this codebase's OWN existing precedent (Phase 10's storefront_discovery_index JSON + generated-column pattern), promote a JSON field to generated+indexed column only when it needs to be queryable; (3) legacy items.category (raw_material/packaging/product/supplies/service) does not map to new category (food/service/retail) -- resolved by treating all migrated items as generic sellable products, explicitly deferring the raw-material-vs-finished-good distinction to a future not-yet-scoped DGFY<->IMS contract, since legacy only conflates both concerns because DGFY was historically built as a module inside the SKUpervisor Food Manufacturing IMS; (4) inventory_movements' simpler taxonomy (restock/loss/adjustment/sale/booking, single stock_count, no per-location breakdown) is intentionally sufficient for DGFY's finished-goods-selling need -- legacy's manufacturing-only movement types and multi-location/FIFO/batch tracking are out of scope, not a gap to close

decisions.decision: Real GHCR :beta images used for backend/dgfy-api/frontend on the rehearsal EC2 (not :develop) -- corrected mid-session after read-only recon of the actual production server (ssh alias: dgfy) confirmed :beta is what's really deployed.
decisions.rationale: Fidelity to the real deployed artifact matters more than convenience for a beta-parity proof.

decisions.decision: Frontend rebuilt locally on the EC2 (not pulled from GHCR) with VITE_DGFY_AUTH_URL/VITE_SKUPERVISOR_BASE_URL left empty.
decisions.rationale: The :beta frontend bakes these to beta.dgfy.ph at Vite build time; no runtime config can override a compiled-in value. Source confirmed byte-identical to develop's tip (git diff origin/develop HEAD -- backend/ frontend/ is empty), so building from this repo IS building from develop.

decisions.decision: products schema gets 6 new typed columns (sku_code, cost_per_unit, vat_type, senior_pwd_discount_eligible, description, unit_of_measure) plus one attributes JSON column for everything else variable.
decisions.rationale: The 6 are universal to any item type (not IMS-manufacturing-specific); the rest varies too much across item types (food nutrition vs. future apparel sizing etc.) to justify rigid columns or tables, and EAV is a known anti-pattern. Follows this codebase's own existing JSON+generated-column precedent (storefront_discovery_index, Phase 10).

decisions.decision: Legacy items.category (5 values, raw-material-centric) does not map to new products.category (3 values, food/service/retail) -- migrated items are treated as generic sellable products; the raw-material-vs-finished-good distinction is explicitly deferred to a future DGFY<->IMS integration contract.
decisions.rationale: User's own framing: DGFY's items table only lives inside the IMS's schema because DGFY was historically built as a module inside the SKUpervisor Food Manufacturing IMS -- this migration is re-importing DGFY's own sale items, not building the DGFY<->IMS contract itself.

decisions.decision: inventory_movements' simpler 5-type taxonomy and single stock_count (no per-location breakdown, no FIFO/batch) is treated as intentionally sufficient, not a gap.
decisions.rationale: Legacy's richer model (multi-location transfers, production_consumption/output, FIFO batches, weighted-average-cost) is manufacturing-grade tracking that belongs to IMS, not to DGFY selling a finished product -- matches PROJECT.md's own already-documented 'Comprehensive Inventory / external IMS integration -- contract not yet defined technically' Out of Scope entry.
